title: repair segmented egress policy mismatch causing intermittent cross-tenant DNS/egress leakage
creator: Ana Ribeiro
description: High-severity customer escalations reported that dedicated tenants experienced intermittent DNS and egress cross-talk after autoscaler events and peering failovers. Symptoms: tenants able to resolve private DNS names from other tenants and outbound flows occasionally observed with wrong egress NAT IP. Impact affected a small subset of Dedicated clusters running v1.21 dataplane image, but produced severe confidentiality concerns for affected customers. This ticket tracks investigation, hotfix rollout, and follow-ups to prevent recurrence.
reproducible_steps: 1) Provision a dedicated tenant with segmented egress policy and per-tenant egress gateway assignment enabled
2) Create a second tenant with internal-only DNS records and a distinct egress NAT pool
3) Trigger a scale-to-zero and back (autoscaler) on nodes hosting tenant dataplane pods multiple times

4) Observe that in ~1-2% of runs the scaled-up dataplane reattaches to an existing connection tracking namespace with stale iptables MARK rules and can resolve peer tenant DNS and egress via wrong gateway
5) Reproduction is more likely when the cluster experiences rapid node churn or when VPC peering routes are reconverging
incident_timeline: 2025-11-16 09:12 UTC: First customer Slack escalation received (Enterprise X). Reported private DNS for tenant B resolvable from tenant A
2025-11-16 10:05 UTC: On-call infra team triaged; observed anomalous conntrack entries and overlapping iptables MARK rules on node-07
2025-11-16 14:30 UTC: Confirmed correlation with recent autoscaler scale events and with peering route flaps in region-us-west2
2025-11-17 02:20 UTC: Emergency mitigation: forced eviction of affected dataplane pods, run egress rebind script which cleared stale marks, incidents remediated for those clusters
2025-11-20 18:00 UTC: Root-cause hypothesis validated in staging: assignment controller race leads to temporary reuse of internal mark values across tenants
2025-11-26 11:45 UTC: Patch developed to introduce atomic update + per-tenant mark namespace and reconciliation loop
2025-12-03 07:30 UTC: Hotfix rolled to Canary clusters, metrics monitored for 72 hours
2026-01-08 17:10 UTC: Customer audit completed with affected accounts, remediation steps and timeline shared
2026-01-18 09:00 UTC: Submit PR for production hardening changes and tests; this ticket moved to In Review
root_cause: The tenant egress assignment controller produced non-deterministic mark allocations during rapid rebinds. When a dataplane pod restarted concurrently with an egress reassignment, the controller sometimes emitted iptables updates that overlapped previously-used MARK ranges because we reused mark IDs without coordinating per-node ownership. Combined with a delayed conntrack namespace cleanup on kernel 5.10 variants, this allowed packets from one tenant to be accepted and NATed by another tenant's gateway for a short window.
fix_summary: 1) Controller: allocate mark namespaces deterministically per-tenant and persist mapping in a leader-backed shard so rebinds are atomic. 2) Dataplane: ensure conntrack cleanup completes before allowing egress bind; add backoff + health check. 3) Add reconciliation that detects overlapping marks and repairs in-flight. 4) Add unit + e2e tests that simulate rapid scale events and peering flaps. 5) Ship runtime-1.24.3 hotfix with the controller and dataplane patches.
affected_customers: SaaS Y (eu-central) - reported intermittent DNS leakage
customer_communications: 2025-11-17: initial acknowledgement and mitigation instructions provided (support#4452)
2025-12-10: status update with interim mitigations and ETA for hotfix (account reps notified)
2026-01-09: post-remediation report and recommended verification steps shared; customers offered audit of tenant configs
rollback_plan: If the hotfix triggers regressions, rollback to runtime-1.24.2 and revert controller deployment. Emergency script to clear overlapping marks and force egress rebind (scripts/egress_rebind.sh) can be applied cluster-wide as temporary mitigation.
postmortem_actions: Add deterministic mark allocation and persist mapping to leader store (done in PR)
Add e2e chaos tests covering autoscaler + peering + conntrack delays
Improve canary rollout policy to include egress isolation verification for dedicated clusters
Document runbook for support to detect overlapping marks and perform safe remediation
Audit kernels in our dedicated fleet and standardize on conntrack behavior or apply backported fixes
monitoring_changes: Dashboard: Dedicated -> Networking -> Egress Isolation (adds per-tenant mark allocation graph and recent reconciles)
Log alert: suspicious DNS replies originating from internal IP ranges not owned by the tenant
